purpose: Erdafitinib is used to treat a certain type of bladder cancer called urothelial carcinoma that has spread or cannot be removed with surgery. It is specifically for patients whose cancer has a particular gene change called an FGFR2 or FGFR3 mutation. Your doctor will run a special test to confirm your cancer has this gene change before prescribing this medicine.
how_it_works: Think of cancer cells as having a faulty 'on switch' that tells them to keep growing out of control. Erdafitinib works by blocking a specific protein called FGFR that acts like that switch. By blocking FGFR, this medicine helps slow down or stop cancer cells from growing and spreading.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include mouth sores, changes in your nails (such as separation from the nail bed), dry or cracked skin, diarrhea, dry mouth, decreased appetite, changes in taste, fatigue, nausea, low sodium levels in the blood, and eye problems such as dry eyes or blurry vision.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious eye problems, including vision changes or even vision loss — report any eye discomfort, blurry vision, or vision changes to your doctor right away. It can also cause high phosphate levels in the blood, so your doctor will monitor you with regular blood tests and may adjust your dose. Erdafitinib can harm an unborn baby, so both men and women should use effective birth control during treatment and for a period after stopping. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Avoid eating foods very high in phosphate (like dairy and nuts) early in treatment unless told otherwise by your care team.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 8 mg taken by mouth once daily as a single tablet. After about 14 to 21 days, your doctor may increase your dose to 9 mg once daily based on your blood phosphate levels and how well you tolerate the medicine. Take it at the same time each day with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush or split it.
